title: Measuring Cooling Rate in the Lab (Time-Based 'Method of Cooling')
notes: In practice, dθ/dt isn't measured directly — instead, measure the time (t) taken for the temperature to fall across a fixed, identical range for both liquids (e.g. 60°C → 50°C)
Since Δθ is the same for both, substituting these into m₁c₁(dθ/dt)₁ = m₂c₂(dθ/dt)₂ cancels Δθ out, leaving the practical experimental formula: **m₁c₁/t₁ = m₂c₂/t₂**
